agent_name: Sample data: Cedar Lane online shop
greet_message: This is Cedar Lane, a made-up online shop with a year of orders (calendar 2025). Ask about customers, revenue, products, payments or returns, or pick a question below. The data is synthetic and read-only.

database.description: Cedar Lane, a synthetic online shop selling electronics, home goods, apparel, beauty, sports, toys, books and office supplies to consumers and businesses in the United States. Covers calendar year 2025: customers, products and categories, orders and their line items, payments and returns.

suggested_questions: Who are our top five customers by total spend?
How did monthly revenue change across 2025?
Which product categories have the highest return rate?
What share of orders was paid with each payment method?
Which acquisition channel brings customers with the highest average order value?
Show a bar chart of the top five customers by total spend.

tables.products: The product catalogue (120 products). Each product belongs to one category (category_id references categories). list_price is the current selling price and unit_cost what the shop pays for it, both in US dollars. Gross margin of a sale = (order_items.unit_price - products.unit_cost) * quantity.
tables.customers: One row per customer account (2,400). segment is 'consumer' or 'business'. acquisition_channel is how the customer first found the shop: organic_search, paid_search, social, email, referral or marketplace. A customer's name is first_name and last_name together.
tables.orders: One row per order placed in 2025. status is processing, shipped, delivered or cancelled; a cancelled order was never paid and is excluded from revenue and spend. total_amount = subtotal - discount_amount + shipping_fee, in US dollars, and is the order's value. Business definitions: revenue = SUM(total_amount) of orders whose status is not 'cancelled'; a customer's total spend = SUM(total_amount) of their non-cancelled orders; average order value = AVG(total_amount) of non-cancelled orders. Use ordered_at for dates and months.
tables.order_items: The products in each order (order_id references orders, product_id references products). line_total = quantity * unit_price. An order item is 'sold' when its order is not cancelled and 'delivered' when its order's status is 'delivered'.
tables.payments: Payment attempts for orders. status 'captured' is a successful payment; 'failed' attempts are followed by a captured one. Each non-cancelled order has exactly one captured payment, so payment-method shares are counted over captured payments. method is card, paypal, apple_pay, gift_card or bank_transfer.
tables.returns: Return requests for individual order items (order_item_id references order_items). status is approved, rejected or pending; refund_amount is the line total for approved returns and 0 otherwise. Return rate of a group = approved returns / order items on delivered orders, as a percent.
